requirement_text: All first-year applicants must submit results from at least one SAT and/or ACT in order to be considered for admission. We do not require the ACT Writing section or the SAT optional essay. We will not use scores received on your school transcript or via email, fax, or postal service. Official SAT/ACT scores are required of students who enroll at Georgia Tech.
limitations: No minimum or cutoff score is published for general holistic admission -- this is a binary submission requirement (a score must be reported), not a numeric threshold to compare a student's score against. Contrast with the Georgia Tech Scholars Program (REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0014), which DOES publish explicit minimum SAT/ACT section-score thresholds, but only for that separate guaranteed-consideration pathway, not for general admission. No minimum GPA is published anywhere found in this pass either (checked admission.gatech.edu/first-year/, /first-year/application-review, and /first-year/academic-preparation); Georgia Tech's review is explicitly holistic without a stated GPA cutoff for general admission.
researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK (test-optional/required conflict, the top risk flagged for this research pass): the research brief's framing assumed Georgia Tech 'reinstated' standardized testing requirements, implying Georgia Tech itself previously went test-optional and later came back. Direct research does not support that framing for Georgia Tech specifically, and this record corrects it. What actually happened: the University System of Georgia (USG) suspended testing at 23 of its 26 institutions starting in 2020 during the pandemic, but explicitly KEPT testing mandatory throughout at its three most selective institutions -- Georgia Tech, the University of Georgia, and Georgia College & State University (corroborated by capitol-beat.org, insidehighered.com, and ajc.com news coverage of USG Board of Regents decisions; these secondary news sources are cited only as corroborating historical context, not as the basis for the current-policy fact itself, which rests on Georgia Tech's own live page cited as source_url). The 'reinstatement' news from 2024-2026 (capitol-beat.org, insidehighered.com, highereddive.com) refers to OTHER USG institutions (e.g. Augusta University, Georgia Southern, Kennesaw State) restoring testing requirements for the 2026 cycle -- NOT Georgia Tech, which never dropped the requirement in the first place. Checked specifically for a stale/contradicting Georgia Tech UNDERGRADUATE test-optional page still live (the brief's explicit instruction): searched site:admission.gatech.edu for 'test-optional', and found ONLY graduate-level Scheller College of Business MBA test-optional pages (evening-mba and full-time-mba admissions -- a completely separate graduate application process with its own admissions office and applicant pool), plus one Georgia Tech admission-blog post discussing the test-optional trend industry-wide without claiming test-optional status for Georgia Tech itself. No undergraduate first-year test-optional page, current or archived-but-still-live, was found anywhere on a gatech.edu domain. Also checked catalog.gatech.edu/admissions/ugrad/first-year directly, word by word, for the terms 'required'/'optional'/'must submit'/'test-optional': none of these words appear anywhere on that page in connection with SAT/ACT; it only uses softer language ('may self-report... for us to use in file review'). This is under-specification (the catalog page is simply less detailed than admission.gatech.edu's dedicated testing page), not a contradiction, so it is NOT recorded as CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE -- it doesn't assert an opposing policy, it just omits detail found more completely elsewhere on an official Georgia Tech domain. Conclusion: VERIFIED_UNDATED (the live testing-policy page itself does not self-state a cycle year), not CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE -- but the brief's assumed 'reinstated' narrative should be corrected specifically for Georgia Tech. Superscoring: multiple independent secondary sources describe Georgia Tech as superscoring both the SAT and ACT (combining highest section scores across sittings), and the official testing page's own description of 'highest section score' evaluation is consistent with that practice, but the specific word 'superscore' was not found verbatim on admission.gatech.edu itself in this pass -- treat the superscoring characterization as extracted_summary-level confidence, not a quoted term of art from Georgia Tech.

requirement_text: English - 4 Units; Math - 4 Units; Science - 4 Units; Social Science - 3 Units; Foreign Language, American Sign Language or Computer Science - 2 Units. Most applicants exceed these in at least one area.
limitations: These are University System of Georgia (USG) minimum required units, stated on Georgia Tech's own academic-preparation page as the floor Georgia Tech applies. Secondary/aggregator sources (not independently confirmed via official fetch in this pass) additionally describe sub-requirements such as specific course content within the math units (algebra, geometry, precalculus) and a lab-component requirement within the science units -- a direct fetch of admission.gatech.edu/first-year/academic-preparation in this pass explicitly did NOT confirm those sub-clauses (the page states unit counts only), so they are deliberately excluded from requirement_text per the search-discovers-fetch-verifies rule, rather than included on secondary-source authority alone. No minimum GPA is published for general admission (see REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0001's limitations).
researcher_notes: USG-mandated unit minimums, applicable system-wide rather than Georgia-Tech-specific in origin, but recorded from Georgia Tech's own admissions page (the page Georgia Tech itself directs applicants to), consistent with this record's applies_to and source_url.

requirement_text: Personal Essay: choose one of seven essay prompts provided by Common App. Beginning with the 2026-27 application cycle, the Georgia Tech-specific short-answer/supplemental essay question has been eliminated; only the Common App personal essay is required. Optional (not required): the Common App's Responsibilities and Circumstances section and the Additional Information section may be used to provide contextual information.
researcher_notes: SIGNIFICANT, RECENT POLICY CHANGE directly relevant to this record's own cycle_year=2027: Georgia Tech eliminated its supplemental short-answer essay ('why this major') for the 2026-27 application cycle / Fall 2027 entry, per official announcement at https://news.em.gatech.edu/2026/07/29/admission-supplemental-essay/ (dated 2026-07-29, about one month before this research pass's retrieval date of 2026-08-21). Mary Tipton Woolley, executive director of Undergraduate Admission, is quoted stating 'the supplemental essay was no longer a differentiating factor in our decision-making process.' Checked the live personal-essays page directly for whether it had actually been updated to match the announcement -- i.e. checked for exactly the 'two live official pages disagree' pattern this research pass was warned to expect for test-optional policy, generalized here to essay policy -- and confirmed CONSISTENT rather than conflicting: the live page shows only the Common App essay with no Georgia Tech-specific prompt, matching the announcement. No stale contradicting page (e.g. an old cached page still listing the eliminated short-answer prompt) was found. Recorded as VERIFIED_CURRENT, not CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE.

requirement_text: Students have the option to send recommendations to Georgia Tech. This is completely optional. We can only accept up to three recommendations per applicant: We can accept one recommendation from a high school counselor. We can accept up to two teacher recommendations. A teacher of a core academic subject (English, math, science, social science, or foreign language) is likely the best option.
limitations: Recommendations must arrive by approximately two weeks after the applicant's own application submission deadline (a relative, not a fixed calendar, deadline -- tied to whichever round, EA1/EA2/RD, the applicant used). Georgia Tech 'cannot accept' recommendation letters from anyone outside a counselor or core-academic-subject teacher (e.g. not from coaches, employers, or family friends) per the same page.
researcher_notes: CORRECTED FIGURE: an earlier-stage web search (not a direct official fetch) suggested a cap of 'up to four' letters, sourced from a third-party admissions-consulting aggregator (CollegeVine) -- this figure was NOT used. The official admission.gatech.edu/first-year/recommendations page, fetched directly, states the cap as THREE (one counselor + up to two teachers), and that is the figure recorded here. Flagging this discrepancy explicitly as a concrete, realized example of why this lane's evidence rules exclude aggregator-sourced numbers in favor of direct official fetches.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (includes Home Edition & My Best): 69 if taken prior to 2026 (minimum); 79 if taken prior to 2026 (recommended).
limitations: This is the University System of Georgia (USG) system-wide floor, not a Georgia-Tech-specific page. USG's own policy states 'institutions may set higher required scores than those listed,' so an institution-specific higher minimum is technically possible -- but Georgia Tech's own international first-year admissions page (admission.gatech.edu/international/first-year), fetched directly in this pass, does NOT publish any Georgia-Tech-specific number and simply directs applicants to 'USG approved methods.' This USG-wide figure is therefore Georgia Tech's actual operative undergraduate first-year requirement, not merely a hypothetical fallback. Do NOT confuse with Georgia Tech's GRADUATE school minimum (TOEFL iBT total >=90, minimum 19 per section, per grad.gatech.edu), which is set independently by the Graduate Studies office for a completely different applicant population and does NOT apply to first-year undergraduate admission -- conflating these two numbers was an active, realized risk during this research pass (several early-stage web searches for 'Georgia Tech undergraduate TOEFL' returned the graduate 90/19 figures), corrected only by fetching admission.gatech.edu/international/first-year directly rather than trusting search-snippet framing.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK: this is the pre-2026-rescale TOEFL iBT figure on ETS's original 0-120 scale, explicitly bounded by USG's own page to tests 'taken prior to 2026' -- unambiguous. USG publishes only an overall/total minimum on this row, no per-subtest minimum, so this does NOT exhibit the Glasgow-style partial-unsatisfiability defect documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md. See companion record REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0006 for the post-rescale (1-6 scale) figure from the same source line. NAMED-INCLUSION note (mirror of the named-exclusion trap, finding #3 in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md): USG's row explicitly includes 'Home Edition & My Best' (i.e. TOEFL MyBest / superscored) editions as ACCEPTED -- the OPPOSITE of University of Edinburgh's explicit exclusion ('We do not accept TOEFL MyBest Score'). Recorded explicitly per the evidence-discipline instruction that named exclusions AND inclusions on score provenance should be captured, not just exclusions.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (includes Home Edition & My Best): 3.5 (minimum); 4.0 (recommended). [Scores on ETS's rescaled 1-6 band, effective for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026.]
limitations: Same source-page limitations as REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0005 (USG system-wide floor; Georgia Tech's own international/first-year page publishes no stricter number; do not confuse with the separate graduate-school TOEFL minimum).
researcher_notes: Same source table row as REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0005. USG's own page does NOT explain the reason for two TOEFL figures or explicitly mention ETS's 21 January 2026 rescale -- the rescale context (ETS moving TOEFL iBT to a 1-6 band, average rather than sum of section scores, per ETS's own announcement already documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md) is supplied from this research lane's own prior finding, not from USG's page itself, hence text_fidelity is extracted_summary rather than verbatim_quoted for this record specifically. USG's own parenthetical '(69 if taken prior to 2026)' on the same table row is what anchors this second figure (3.5) as the post-cutover value, even without USG spelling out the mechanism. No per-subtest minimum is published on this row either, so no Glasgow-style partial-unsatisfiability defect.

requirement_text: IELTS Academic (including IELTS Online and One Skill Retake): 6 (minimum); 6.5 (recommended).
limitations: Same USG-system-wide-floor limitation as REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0005/0006 (Georgia Tech's own page does not publish a stricter institution-specific IELTS minimum for undergraduate admission).
researcher_notes: NAMED-EXCLUSION TRAP CHECK (finding #3 in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md): USG's policy explicitly INCLUDES 'IELTS Online and One Skill Retake' as accepted formats -- the OPPOSITE of University of Edinburgh's explicit exclusion ('We do not accept IELTS One Skill Retake to meet our English language requirements'). Recorded explicitly since this research pass was specifically briefed to check for named exclusions/inclusions on score provenance; IELTS's 0-9 band scale itself is unaffected by the TOEFL rescale.

requirement_text: Cambridge English Scale Score - which can be demonstrated in B2 First (First Certificate in English - FCE), C1 Advanced (Certificate in Advanced English - CAE) or C2 Proficiency (Certificate of Proficiency in English - CPE): 169 (minimum); 177 (recommended).
researcher_notes: Confirmed unaffected by the TOEFL rescale, consistent with the scale audit in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md (the Cambridge English Scale is a distinct, unchanged scale).

requirement_text: Other USG-approved methods to satisfy the English proficiency requirement: PTE Academic minimum 53 (recommended 58); SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing minimum 480; ACT English minimum 17; MET (Michigan English Test) minimum 55 (recommended 59); EIKEN Pre-1 level or higher; GCSE English grade C or better; GCE A-Level English grade C or better; IGCSE and O-Level English grade D or better; EdExcel International A-Levels/IGCSE grade D or better; completion of an approved USG campus-based ESL program; degree completion where English was the sole official language of academic instruction; equivalent of English 1101/1102 with grade C or better at an accredited U.S. institution; direct college-level English placement without corequisites.
limitations: Multiple distinct scales bundled into one record (PTE, SAT, ACT, MET, EIKEN, UK qualifications, alternative pathways) since none has its own dedicated test_scale enum value in this schema besides TOEFL/IELTS/Cambridge/SAT -- the SAT ERW>=480 line specifically could be split into its own record with test_scale SAT_1600 if a future pass wants that granularity; left combined here as a proportionate scoping choice for a secondary/alternative-methods list. Same USG-system-wide-floor limitation as the other English-proficiency records in this batch.
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION, high value: Georgia Tech's own international first-year page (admission.gatech.edu/international/first-year, fetched directly) states the Duolingo English Test is welcomed as a SUPPLEMENTARY material but explicitly 'do[es] not satisfy [the] USG requirement' -- i.e. Duolingo, despite being one of the most commonly submitted English tests by international applicants generally, does NOT satisfy Georgia Tech's actual requirement and is 'considered in holistic review' only alongside a qualifying method from this list. This is exactly the named-exclusion trap category from scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md (a commonly-submitted, qualifying-looking score the institution will not accept as satisfying the requirement) and should NOT be evaluated as met from a Duolingo score alone.

requirement_text: International applicants are welcome to submit supplementary materials such as the Duolingo English Test, and are encouraged to pursue an unscripted interview through InitialView or Vericant.
limitations: This is an optional supplementary/supporting material, not a required application component -- do not evaluate a missing interview as not_met. Minor wording tension (short of CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE) found and flagged for human review: Georgia Tech's general 'Application Review Process' page (admission.gatech.edu/first-year/application-review) lists 'Interview requirements (international applicants only)' as one bullet among its holistic-review factors, phrasing that could be misread as implying interviews are mandatory for international applicants. The international-specific page (this record's source, more directly on point) clearly frames the interview as encouraged/welcomed rather than mandatory ('welcome to submit... encouraged to pursue'). This record follows the more specific, more directly on-topic page. Neither page states the literal opposite of the other, so this was not escalated to CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE, but the softer bullet-list phrasing on the general review page is worth a human glance.

requirement_text: International students are not eligible for federal or state financial aid programs, and institutional scholarships administered by Georgia Tech's Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid (OSFA) are often not awarded to international students.
limitations: 'Often not awarded' is Georgia Tech's own hedge, not an absolute 'never' -- some institutional scholarship pathways may remain open to international students in specific cases. This record should not be read as a categorical bar on ALL institutional aid, only on federal/state aid (categorically barred by law) and MOST institutional aid (not categorically, but practically, barred per Georgia Tech's own wording).
researcher_notes: Alternative options Georgia Tech does offer to international students per the same page: privately-funded loan programs (most requiring 'a creditworthy co-signer who is a U.S. citizen or permanent resident with a permanent U.S. address'), an Emergency Tuition Loan administered by OSFA for unforeseen financial hardship (first-come, first-served), Bursar's-office payment plans for temporary payment delays, and general guidance from the Office of International Education. None of these are need-based grant aid. See deadline records DL-2026-08-21-GAT0010 and DL-2026-08-21-GAT0011 for the related financial-aid application deadline findings.

requirement_text: First-year application fee: $75 (domestic); $85 (international). Non-refundable. Fee waiver available via the Common Application profile section for applicants who: have received or are eligible to receive an ACT or SAT testing fee waiver; are enrolled in or eligible to participate in the federal free or reduced price lunch program (FRPL); have annual family income within the income eligibility guidelines set by the USDA Food and Nutrition Service; are enrolled in a federal, state, or local program that aids students from low-income families (e.g. TRIO programs such as Upward Bound); have a family that receives public assistance; live in federally subsidized public housing, a foster home, or are homeless; or are a ward of the state or an orphan. First-generation college students (U.S. citizens or Permanent Residents whose parents did not complete a four-year college degree) and applicants residing in FEMA-declared disaster areas may separately request a fee waiver through the Georgia Tech questions section of the Common Application.

[APS Scholars Program] Be named either the valedictorian or the salutatorian of any of the accredited public high schools or charter high schools in Atlanta Public Schools (APS). Be in overall good standing with APS at point of graduation. Meet all stated Board of Regents academic requirements for entry into a research university. Successfully complete a math course at the pre-calculus level or above during high school (College Precalculus/USG Math 1113 for dual enrollment students; note College Algebra does not fulfill this requirement). Apply for first-year admission to Georgia Tech and submit all supporting documents by either the Early Action Plan or the Regular Decision application deadline. Guarantees acceptance and covers four-year in-state tuition and mandatory fees for four academic years (eight semesters), contingent on maintaining good academic standing.
limitations: Narrow eligibility scope: Atlanta Public Schools district only (a small subset of Georgia residents) -- not to be confused with the broader, state-wide Georgia Tech Scholars Program (REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0014), which uses similar valedictorian/salutatorian class-rank logic but different eligibility criteria (explicit SAT/ACT score thresholds; any SACS-accredited Georgia high school with 50+ graduates, not just APS) and different guaranteed benefits (a $2,500-$5,000/year need-based scholarship, not full guaranteed admission plus full tuition).
researcher_notes: The source page does not explicitly state whether admission is fully automatic or still passes through some verification step -- it says the program 'uses the information supplied on the application' to identify scholars, which reads as an eligibility-confirmation step rather than the kind of holistic comparative review the general applicant pool receives. This record does not assert full automaticity beyond what the source itself states.

requirement_text: [Georgia Tech Scholars Program] Valedictorian or salutatorian of any of the state's SACS-accredited high schools with more than 50 graduates by April 1 of the senior year, with school rank and standing verified by a school official. Meet all stated Board of Regents academic requirements for entry into a research university. Minimum test scores: SAT Evidence Based Reading & Writing >= 480 AND SAT Math >= 530, OR ACT English >= 17 AND ACT Math Test >= 21. Successfully complete a math course at the pre-calculus or Dual Enrollment pre-calculus level or above during high school. (Note: College Algebra does not fulfill this requirement.) Apply for first-year admission by either the Early Action or Regular Decision application deadline.
scope: Georgia valedictorians/salutatorians statewide (any SACS-accredited Georgia high school with 50+ graduates)
limitations: This is one of the only places Georgia Tech publishes an explicit numeric SAT/ACT threshold anywhere found in this research pass -- general holistic first-year admission (REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0001) has no published minimum. This threshold applies only to Georgia Tech Scholars Program eligibility, a specific guaranteed-consideration pathway for valedictorians/salutatorians, not to general admission. The ACT-based alternative threshold (English>=17 AND Math>=21) has no corresponding test_scale enum value in this schema (only SAT_1600 is available for SAT/ACT-family thresholds) -- test_scale is set to SAT_1600 to reflect the SAT branch of this either/or threshold only; the ACT branch is preserved in requirement_text but not separately scale-tagged.
researcher_notes: Financial benefit is a Val-Sal Scholarship of up to $2,500/year for Georgia residents with demonstrated financial need (annual family income <= $75,000; up to $5,000/year if also Federal Pell Grant-eligible), NOT full tuition -- do not confuse with the separate APS Scholars Program (REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0013), which guarantees full admission plus full in-state tuition, but only for the narrower Atlanta Public Schools population. The source text describes 'admission' being offered to eligible students but does not use the words 'guaranteed' or 'automatic' for the admission component (unlike APS Scholars' clearer 'acceptance' guarantee language); this record does not overclaim automaticity beyond the source's own wording.

requirement_text: Scholarship consideration requires you to apply through an Early Action plan and meet the appropriate Early Action plan deadlines.
limitations: Applies to institute-wide merit scholarship consideration (e.g. Stamps President's Scholars Program, Georgia Tech Gold Scholarship, per secondary corroboration not independently fetched in this pass) -- does NOT affect admission eligibility itself; a Regular Decision applicant can still be admitted, just without merit-scholarship consideration. Not a binding commitment of any kind (does not obligate the student to enroll or to forgo applying elsewhere) -- distinguished here explicitly from the binding/exclusivity constraint category this research pass was briefed to watch for. This is a pure eligibility/timing gate, not a binding contractual commitment, so it does NOT get the special 'needs human review before converting to structured_rule' treatment that a genuine binding constraint (see REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0016's notes) would require.
researcher_notes: Directly responsive to this pass's brief regarding whether Georgia Tech's Early Action carries binding or exclusivity language: this scholarship-eligibility gate is the ONLY genuine EA-linked constraint found anywhere in this research pass. See REQ-2026-08-21-GAT0016 for the full binding/exclusivity investigation and its negative result.

source_authority_note: commonapp.org fails looksOfficial() (no .edu/.ac./.gov suffix) despite being the official Common Application platform through which Georgia Tech itself exclusively accepts first-year applications -- needs the officialDomains-provenance fix documented in source-authority-gap.md, not a lowered evidence bar. Analogous to UCAS for UK admissions.
researcher_notes: BINDING/EXCLUSIVITY INVESTIGATION, directly responsive to this pass's brief: thoroughly checked whether Georgia Tech's Early Action carries a genuine binding or exclusivity (restrictive/single-choice) constraint, parallel to Yale's Restrictive Early Action or a binding Early Decision program, and found NONE. Evidence: (1) Common App's own platform page for Georgia Tech (this record's source, an official_application_system) explicitly labels the round 'Early Action (non-binding)' directly next to the round name; (2) direct fetches of admission.gatech.edu/apply/ and admission.gatech.edu/first-year/deadlines contain zero instances of the words 'binding', 'exclusive', 'restrict', 'commit', or any phrase mentioning other colleges/schools/institutions; (3) a guessed dedicated URL admission.gatech.edu/first-year/early-action returns 404 (no such standalone FAQ page exists to check further); (4) multiple independent secondary/consulting sources (not used as the basis for this record's core claim, cited only as corroborating color) separately describe both EA1 and EA2 as fully non-restrictive, consistent with (1)-(3). Conclusion: Georgia Tech's Early Action (both EA1 and EA2, see DL-2026-08-21-GAT0001 and DL-2026-08-21-GAT0004) is non-binding, and no exclusivity restriction was found anywhere despite specific, thorough searching. Per this brief's explicit instruction to write a binding-constraint companion record 'only if Georgia Tech's EA genuinely has such a restriction' -- since none was found, no such companion record was created. This record instead documents the non-binding status itself and the negative search result for a restriction, so a future pass does not have to redo this check from scratch.
